channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Effectiveness of a Personalized Robot-Assisted Trunk and Lower Limb Rehabilitation in Patients with Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=40) found that adding personalized robot-assisted trunk and lower limb training to conventional rehabilitation significantly improved Functional Ambulatory Category (FAC) scores in patients with chronic stroke over 3 months.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical and mental health-related quality of life outcomes of non-pharmacological interventions in early multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found non-pharmacological interventions to improve physical and mental health-related quality of life in adults with early-stage multiple sclerosis and minimal disability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the effectiveness and optimal dosage of physical exercise on cognitive function in older adults with Alzheimer's disease.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Foot-Targeted Rehabilitation for Pronation-Related Anterior Knee Pain: A Two-Phase Case-Control Study and Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Manual Therapy Versus Neuromuscular Training Each With Augmented Low-Dye Taping.
item.description: A two-phase study found that neuromuscular training with augmented low-dye taping (NMT + ALDT) was more effective in the short term for pronation-related anterior knee pain compared to routine physiotherapy care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of In-Clinic Rehabilitation vs. Home-Based Telerehabilitation for Adults with MS in the Deep South: The TEAMS Cluster Randomized Trial.
item.description: The TEAMS cluster-randomized trial of 759 adults with MS found no significant difference in effectiveness between a 12-week complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) program delivered in-clinic by a therapist (DirectCAM, n=382) versus self-initiated at home via telerehabilitation (TeleCAM, n=377).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Additive Effects of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation on Robotic Therapy for Upper Extremity Recovery After Chronic Ischemic Stroke: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Sham-Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial (N=36) found that adding repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) or transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to robotic therapy did not provide additional benefits for upper extremity motor and functional recovery in patients with chronic ischemic stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Dizziness, Balance, and Postural Stability in Adult Patients With Chronic Peripheral Vestibular Dizziness.
item.description: A double-blind RCT with 56 adults with chronic vestibular dizziness found that repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with vestibular rehabilitation (VR) significantly improved dizziness, balance, and postural stability over 8 weeks compared to sham stimulation + VR.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of sportsmetrics training on biomechanical and functional performance outcomes related to ACL injury risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis confirmed the positive effects of SportsMetrics training on ACL injury-related biomechanical deficits and functional performance outcomes in athletes.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Clinically interpretable prediction models of stroke functional outcomes: A national cohort study of adults in inpatient rehabilitation facilities in the US.
item.description: A national retrospective cohort study (n=43,745) of US stroke patients in inpatient rehabilitation facilities developed clinically interpretable machine learning models to predict self-care and mobility function at discharge using IRF-PAI variables.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial (n=50) demonstrated that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the dermal elastic coefficient and limb circumference in patients with severe hyper-dependency limb oedema compared to 0% tension taping by day 9.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Incidence and risk factors for rotator cuff retear after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair in middle-aged and older patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the incidence and risk factors for rotator cuff retear after arthroscopic repair in middle-aged and older patients.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Bidirectional association between injuries and mental health symptoms among elite athletes: a systematic review
item.description: A systematic review of 25 studies found a bidirectional association between musculoskeletal injuries and mental health symptoms among elite athletes, indicating that mental health symptoms can precede injury, and injury can lead to subsequent mental health symptoms.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Mental health in elite athletes: International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026)
item.description: The updated International Olympic Committee consensus statement (2026) emphasizes that mental health symptoms and disorders are common in elite athletes, may be sport-related, and impact performance, recommending routine screening and monitoring.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Short-term inspiratory muscle training, aerobic exercise, and detraining in women with COPD: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial in women with COPD found that short-term inspiratory muscle training (IMT), aerobic exercise (AE), and combined IMT+AE all significantly improved inspiratory muscle strength, exercise capacity, and quality of life, with effects diminishing after a detraining period.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Responsiveness, Smallest Detectable Change, and Minimal Important Change of the Turkish Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory-20 Following Pelvic Floor Muscle Training.
item.description: A multicenter retrospective study of 200 women with pelvic floor dysfunction found the Turkish Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory-20 (PFDI-20) to be responsive to pelvic floor muscle training, establishing its smallest detectable change (SDC) and minimal important change (MIC).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Relief increases select shoulder muscle activity, following subacromial injection in subacromial pain syndrome.
item.description: This study investigated the effects of immediate and long-term pain reduction on shoulder muscle activation in 21 individuals with subacromial pain syndrome, finding that a subacromial injection led to increased select shoulder muscle activity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reliability and construct validity of three movement-evoked pain methods in individuals with knee osteoarthritis.
item.description: This study evaluated the reliability and construct validity of three movement-evoked pain calculation methods using performance-based tests in 111 individuals with knee osteoarthritis, finding varying levels of reliability and validity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Feasibility and acceptability of the breakfast group intervention BISTRo for stroke survivors in acute rehabilitation.
item.description: A mixed-methods feasibility study evaluated the BISTRo breakfast group intervention for 16 stroke survivors in UK acute rehabilitation, finding it feasible and acceptable to both patients and multidisciplinary staff.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Methodological characteristics of perturbation-based balance training in healthy older adults: A scoping review.
item.description: This scoping review mapped the methodological features of mechanically induced perturbation-based balance training interventions in healthy older adults, analyzing studies from inception through April 2025 across multiple databases.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of functional versus conventional Physiotherapy-Based pain management on symptoms, psychological outcomes, and quality of life in women with Bladder Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=28) found that functional physiotherapy (pain science education, cognition-targeted exercises) improved symptoms, psychological outcomes, and quality of life in women with Bladder Pain Syndrome compared to conventional TENS.
item.author: PubMed
